receipt.public_excerpt: Large language models (LLMs) are powerful but static; they lack mechanisms to adapt their weights in response to new tasks, knowledge, or examples.

evidence_items.explanation: Researchers describe standard LLMs as static, without built-in ways to adapt their weights. This matches the present-tense part of the claim at the time.

receipt.public_excerpt: Through supervised finetuning (SFT), these self-edits result in persistent weight updates, enabling lasting adaptation.

evidence_items.explanation: A research prototype shows an LLM steering its own lasting weight updates. The authors call it 'a promising step', not a deployed capability, so it is not a decisive refutation under the stated rule.
